text:
alex: FYI we had a pretty nasty eviction window in us-west2 last night — ~2h where interactive latency spiked because a handful of preemptible GPUs were reclaimed at once. tracking the timeline now but wanted to capture ideas here

infra-bot: [alert] 2025-11-17T03:12:08Z spot-interruption us-west2: 14 preemptible-nvidia-a100 reclaimed (zone: us-west2-c) :warning:

maya: ugh. saw the spikes in the dashboard. P95 tail went from 120ms -> 780ms for chat sessions. interactive queue basically stalled waiting for new nodes.

jordan: can you paste the batch vs interactive demand plot? curious how much batch was running at the same time

alex: attaching quick summary: interactive pool size = 12 nodes (mixed nvidia-a100 preemptible + 3 on-demand for control plane). batch had ~60 preemptible-only workers running large finetune jobs.

sasha: that's the pattern we've seen before: batch eats spot pool headroom then an interruption happens and the autoscaler can't replenish on-demand fast enough. two levers: (1) keep a small on-demand buffer for interactive SLA or (2) shift batch to a different region/off-peak window

kevin: +1 on buffer. also thinking about priority-aware bin-packing in the scheduler. interactive pods should be allowed to preempt batch pods immediately (fast reclaim) and batch should be tolerant to restarts.

maya: i prototyped a config for that a while back — priority classes + preemptionPolicy + a small warm pool. sample config:

```
queues:
  interactive:
    priority: 100
    min_replicas: 6
    on_demand_reserve: 3
    max_latency_ms: 200
  batch:
    priority: 10
    min_replicas: 0
    preemptible_fraction: 0.95
    offpeak_window: "02:00-08:00"
```

sasha: that looks good. question: on_demand_reserve:3 — is that per-zone or global? we need per-zone for region failures

maya: per-zone, yes. we used nodeAffinity rules to spread the reserve across zones. that keeps interactive capacity when a single zone is hit.

jordan: what about using mixed-instance-pools with different GPU types? e.g., prefer a100 preemptible for batch but fall back to v100 on-demand for interactive. cost goes up a bit but latency stability might be worth it for customers with strict SLAs.

alex: cost tradeoff — our rough calc: having a 3-on-demand-per-zone buffer increases monthly GPU spend by ~18% for the affected clusters but reduces major incident MTTR and avoids lost customer calls. Batch shift to cheaper regions reduces net cost but increases egress+storage transfer ops.

kevin: can we be smarter: autoscaler policy that uses recent interruption rates to tune reserve size? e.g., if preemptible_interruption_rate > 0.4 over last 24h, bump reserve by +2 per zone automatically

ops-runbook: suggested playbook excerpt:
1) infra-bot alerts on >10 interruptions in 1h in a zone
2) autoscaler: temporarily increase on_demand_reserve by 2 per zone for 4h
3) move low-priority batch jobs to alternate region or pause non-critical retraining
4) notify customers in slack channel and open a short incident ticket if interactive P95 > 400ms

maya: we should also adjust scheduling for off-peak batch. our workload profile shows many retrains run during business hours. if we move a chunk to 02:00-08:00 local time we can exploit lower spot contention and lower demand.

sasha: region constraints: some customers can't move data out of eu-west1, so we need a region-aware policy: force more on-demand in regulated regions and be more aggressive with spot in non-regulated.

jordan: agreed. also consider a fallback model strategy: serve interactive from a smaller quantized variant if GPUs become scarce, that gives graceful degradation rather than hard failures.

alex: action items I vote for:
- implement priority-aware scheduler changes (kevin + sasha)
- add autoscaler rule for dynamic reserve based on recent interruption rate (kevin)
- schedule batch shift recommendations and run a one-week pilot for off-peak enforcement (maya + jordan)
- update runbook with the ops-runbook steps (sasha)

kevin: i'll open a PR with the autoscaler change and a simulator to test different interruption thresholds. will include flamegraphs of latency under scenarios.

maya: i'll prepare the pilot and a small dashboard panel that shows reserve size vs interruption rate vs cost delta for the pilot cluster.

infra-bot: [info] created incident ticket INC-2025-4321 for interactive latency spike; assigned to @alex @sasha :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks all. let's reconvene in 48h after the pilot runs to check numbers. :thumbsup:

kevin: noted. I'll tag the PR with "autoscaler-interruption-reserve" and link it here when ready.

jordan: if anyone wants to try the preemption-tolerant training wrapper i added (it checkpoint+resume quickly) ping me and I'll deploy it to a test batch pool. makes batch much less fragile to evictions.

sasha: ping on the runbook update as a PR in ops/playbooks/runbooks/eviction-handling.md

alex: closing loop — last_message_ts set. thanks everyone."
